summary: A pyproject ruff per-file-ignore or coverage omit glob matching no tracked file, a deptry DEP002 ignore for an undeclared distribution, or a first-party mypy override matching no module fails the build. Boilerplate patterns are skipped; the reasoned allow list (DEFAULT_EXEMPTIONS, cupy) is accepted.
changelog: - New gate `tool_config_dead_entries` (hard, no advisory mode): a ruff per-file-ignore or coverage omit glob matching no tracked file, a deptry DEP002 ignore naming an undeclared distribution, or a first-party mypy override matching no module now fails. `**/` matches zero or more directories; a DEP002 entry for cupy is a reasoned exemption.
owner_actions: Add a [[gate]] entry for tool_config_dead_entries to src/py_ci_shared/registry.toml and a README catalogue row (owner-owned files; not edited here).

mlframe: `legacy/*` (no legacy/ directory) and `src/mlframe/**/benchmarks/**` (the directories are `_benchmarks`) are dead entries; the owner should delete or correct them. Both are true positives by the rule.

pyutilz and mlframe: the DEP002 ignore for `py-ci-shared` names a distribution that is not in [project] dependencies (it is installed from requirements-dev.txt). The gate reads only pyproject, so the owner must decide whether the ignore is needed; the gate does not see requirements-dev.txt.
The cupy DEP002 entry in mlframe is accepted by DEFAULT_EXEMPTIONS as an owner-pending reasoned exemption; the raw count with the allow list off includes it.
